quarterly_data.signal: 1.6T TEST ECONOMICS THE CALL DID NOT SIZE: CEO Oleg Khaykin said a 1.6T tester carries 'about 50% price increase' over an 800G box, 'because the components are much more expensive', comparing it to TSMC raising price per wafer 'about 1.5x' each node. Viavi has sold 1.6T equipment 'for over a year, mainly to the developers' (system, module and silicon vendors); production started 'beginning of this year' and adoption is 'maybe third inning for 1.6T, second, third inning, depending on who you are talking to'. The box is backward compatible - one 1.6T tester can test four 400G modules, two 800G or a 1.6T - so cost per bit falls even though cost per box rises, and one high-performance tester can service multiple production lines at once. Content per test is also rising: 400G was laser/dispersion/power in-out, 800G adds precise laser and insertion-loss measurement, and 'as you go to 1.6T, it is a whole new ballgame... a lot more functional test on the line'. On share, of the top 5 transceiver manufacturers Viavi works with all of them, engagement is 'very high with probably 4 out of 5', and with numbers 1, 2 and 3 'we are very much in all of their labs'.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.6T tester about 50% price increase versus 800G (TSMC node analogy about 1.5x); engagement very high with 4 out of 5 of the top 5 transceiver makers

quarterly_data.signal: CPO TEST - TIMING AND WHERE VIAVI SITS: Khaykin said Viavi has been working on a CPO test 'now for well over 12 to close to 2 years. We are now started shipping, I would say even this quarter is early shipments.' Test capacity is facilitized ahead of demand and the next increment is added at about '60%, 70% utilization'. CPO pulls Viavi into semiconductor test next to Advantest, Teradyne and FormFactor - the configuration is an IC tester plus a prober plus an optical rack, all interconnected - and he expects a HIGHER share for Viavi there than in pluggables because Viavi sells an automatable integrated platform with '2,500 SKUs' of measurement modules rather than a point solution. Content per port rises sharply: pluggable is power, dispersion and insertion loss, CPO is multiple insertions plus extensive functional test, with known-good-die, optical-engine and interconnect-platform insertions all before the ASIC and memory go on a module worth 'thousands of dollars' - skip them and 'you will be throwing away tens of millions of dollars'.
quarterly_data.figure: CPO test in development well over 12 months to close to 2 years, early shipments this quarter; capacity increments added at 60%, 70% utilization; 2,500 SKUs of measurement modules

quarterly_data.signal: OCS TEST ATTACH RATE QUANTIFIED: Khaykin said some players build in-house equipment but 'anybody who is buying merchant equipment, we are the dominant supplier' for optical circuit switch test. Asked how to convert an OCS TAM into a test opportunity, he said 'depending on the complexity, you'd say 10% of the annual size is what the test and measurement market ought to be' - that figure applies to the higher-end products such as OCS and CPO, and is 'a lower number for transceiver'. He noted OCS demand is not only from module vendors: 'there's also some hyperscalers who do it directly'. The driver is power - 'there's not enough power in the world to power all these data centers' - pushing architectures from electrical to optical. Because the cost of one bad port pair is a bad switch, customers 'test everything to the nth degree', and for a '100 terabit switch, I don't think anybody's going to skip any tests'.
quarterly_data.figure: test and measurement should be about 10% of the annual size of the high-end (OCS, CPO) market, lower for transceivers

quarterly_data.signal: FIELD INSTRUMENTS ARE NOW A DATA-CENTER BUSINESS: Khaykin called it 'one big surprise for us' - the traditional field instrument line is 'today, that business is over 40% data center driven', led by advanced fiber monitoring. Hyperscalers that bought a lot of dark fiber found 'sometimes the fiber worked... but when you turn it on, you find it does not work', so they now put fiber monitoring at the edge and test, qualify and monitor every fiber across the whole build-out, then pick the best-performing fiber when they turn up capacity, using the collected parametrics to predict outages. 'If you ask me who is the state-of-the-art fiber operator today, it would be the hyperscalers.'
quarterly_data.figure: field instrument business over 40% data center driven

quarterly_data.signal: $500M RUN RATE AND, NEW, THE MARGIN AT THAT LEVEL: Khaykin said Viavi will be 'probably not far from $500 million in the December quarter. If demand strengthens up, heck, we may even hit it... we could get very close within the whisker, even this December quarter' - against a fiscal 2028 framing given three months earlier, which GC Ilan Daskal confirmed had already been pulled in on the last call. New here is profitability at that run rate: asked whether a 30% operating margin is in the model at $500 million, Daskal said 'the high 40 is not an unrealistic number to get to when we get to the 500. That is not an unrealistic thinking.' Khaykin added that incremental dollars carry a near-zero tax rate (U.S. jurisdiction plus the NOLs kept from the Lumentum separation, most converted into amortizable assets) and lower interest after the term-loan payoff, so operating leverage is amplified again at the net line.
quarterly_data.figure: $500 million quarterly revenue possible as early as the December quarter; high 40 operating margin when Viavi reaches the 500

quarterly_data.signal: A NEW FIBER-CONNECTOR TEST MARKET AND THE TUCK-IN THAT SERVES IT: Khaykin said hollow-core, multi-core and multi-ribbon cables plugged in '8, 16, 32' at a time are 'opening all new markets now in manufacturing for fiber' - if one fiber in an expensive connector is bad the whole connector is thrown away, so customers now use interferometry on surface quality because at these speeds 'any kind of imperfection can impact the quality of service'. Viavi 'just bought this company called Digital Optical Research Corp, or for short, DORC', an interferometry specialist, and he said that once it is put into Viavi's production test 'it will go from couple million to tens of millions of dollars'. On M&A discipline he said Viavi walked away from a deal announced that day where 'The price paid was 2x more than what we were prepared to pay'.
quarterly_data.figure: hollow-core, multi-core and multi-ribbon connectors of 8, 16, 32 fibers; DORC interferometry to go from couple million to tens of millions of dollars in Viavi production test
